pr_title: sql: fix bug with operations on collated string arrays
pr_body:
Fixes #45703.

This PR fixes a bug caused by how we parse types of
collations. When we parse the case `expr::STRING[] COLLATE en`,
we parse this as `COLLATE(ANNOTATE(expr, STRING[]), en)`, rather
than `ANNOTATE(expr, (STRING COLLATE en)[])`. This causes various
issues in the DistSQL engine where expressions are serialized
to strings and back.

Release note (bug fix): This PR fixes bugs during query execution
related to creating expressions that are arrays of collated strings.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/46745)

Open for suggestions here -- the solution I've put up doesn't quite work (the cast case seems iffy). I'm wondering if I'm taking the wrong approach here. However, it doesn't feel like type-checking is the correct place to do this, because we aren't really parsing the type correctly.
I'll let @otan review, but this needs to be backported to 20.1 and presumably 19.2/19.1.

I don't think this is correct either. It fails casts/assertions on literals --
```
CREATE TABLE t (
  c TEXT COLLATE en_US DEFAULT('empty' COLLATE en_US),
)
```

This breaks because the default expr gets expanded into `'empty':::STRING COLLATE en_US`, and when parsed back we get a type error. Perhaps I need to keep the collation expr as well.
alright seems like i fixed the CI failures. PTAL

> so am i correct in saying that we put these casts in ourselves (from the planner) before executing them on DistSQL? if so it sounds as if the planner should be the fix here, not the parser.

We have to format expressions before sending them to other nodes or serializing them before plsacing them into processor specs. To ensure that we don't lose type information we include the types in all the expressions, hence us trying to print the type of this array of collated strings. This doesn't seem like something we can avoid, but also doesn't seem like a problem postgres would have.
Im going to let this sit a bit more while I think of a better solution.

as discussed, i think the correct solution is to support `(array[a]::text[]) collate en` like postgres does instead of forcing it into the array like `array[a]::(text collate en)[]`

i think it will be a little painful to do but should be alright
@rafiss @otan maybe time to pick this up again?
this is fixed on master / 21.1. not sure by what though.

comments: I've spent some time on this, and it seems somewhere between the optimizer plan to the distsql flow this expression gets serialized and gets marked with `:::String[]` rather than `:::COLLATE...`. I can't seem to figure out where though.
Ok, I've made some progress on this -- I have a feeling we aren't parsing arrays of collations correctly. `a::STRING[] collate de` parses to have a type annotation = string.
